newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, July up on export demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, July up on export demand.

text.p: Indications that there is export demand for U.S. soybeans spurred a slightly higher close in CBOT July soybeans, while new crop months closed lower on weather, traders and analysts said.

"The fact is, that there is still demand around for old crop supplies," said Jerry Gidel, grain analyst with Dean Witter brokerage in Chicago. "The Chinese are buying some meal out there for July, August and September shipment."
There were reports on Tuesday that China bought up to 200,000 tonnes each of soybeans and soymeal this week.
Traders in Beijing said the soy purchases were of U.S. and South American origin, and were for delivery during July through September, traders said.
Weakness in new crop contracts was prompted by forecasts for good growing weather throughout the Midwest, traders said.
"The new crop got shellacked today on weather," said one veteran trader. "The weather is going to be pretty good this week."
Most forecasters see dry weather and warmer temperatures for this week, which are needed to speed crop development.
CBOT July soybeans settled up two cents per bushel at $8.13, and other months were down 2-1/4 to 12 cents.

Planting data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture showed that plantings were well ahead of last year. USDA put plantings at 84 percent complete, ahead of 57 percent last year and the five-year average of 70 percent.
Pressure on November also stemmed from commodity funds going short in that contract, traders said.
"The funds have finished liquidating July and now they're going short in November," said a floor trader. "It's going to be a game for the commercials from now on."
On the day, ABN Amro-Chicago Corp bought four million bushels July, Refco sold 1.5 million July and four million November. Cargill bought one million July and 500,000 September, pit traders said.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock bought 500 November $6.25 puts and sold 500 November $8.00 calls, pit traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 61,000 contracts. That figure compared with Monday's actual volume of 80,543, according to CBOT data.
